title: No simple network-topology measure predicts memory in pathway models

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No simple network-topology measure predicts memory in pathway models

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Across the 35 surveyed BioModels pathway models, the amount of memory showed no significant correlation with mean number of nodes, edges, degree or hubness, so no single network property is indicative of memory.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Additionally, we tested to see if certain network properties, such as mean number of nodes, edges, degree, and hubness were associated with more or less memory and found there were no significant correlations with any of these measures and any memory (see Discussion).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory”. Scope: 35 ODE pathway models from BioModels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.87

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables and statistical test are explicit and the underlying models are public. The claim is resolvable for the surveyed set, with limited power affecting interpretation of nonsignificance.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compute memory capacity and the four stated topology measures for all 35 models, then reproduce the correlation tests with confidence intervals and multiple-testing treatment. Significant robust associations would refute the reported null result.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Low sample size limits power to detect modest correlations.

A null result does not establish that no topology measure is predictive.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.96
discriminating power: 0.8
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Topology is in the SBML files and memory scores can be recomputed, so the correlation test is straightforward. A failure to find a significant correlation in this small curated set does not show that no network property indicates memory. The test is informative only inside the original sample and statistic.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each of the 35 models, pair a memory-count with mean node number, edge number, degree and hubness, and test rank correlations. Significant associations would refute the null result; consistently non-significant correlations would reproduce it, without showing that no structural feature matters.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Thirty-five models give low power, so a non-significant correlation is a weak null.

Hubness and degree definitions, and multiple testing across memory types, are easy to vary.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.5
data existence: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.75
